prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). It proposes TOBT (Target Off Block Time), feasible only if both airside capacity and the ground service path allow it. TOBT is frozen at the horizon unless a rule exception or authorized override is recorded. Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional and Southport keep safety authority. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; Airport Capacity Plan, Acceptance Rate); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; derives CTT (Calculated Takeoff Time)); Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display states proposed/under negotiation/frozen/exempted; frozen change needs revised reason code; shall publish tower readiness changes to authenticated airline/handling users within refresh interval; presents resource feasibility status to AOC and AOR); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; runway order; Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State applies BRR spacing, flags likely CTT misses); Departure Metering Service (sends CTT to TSM); Flight Data Exchange; North/South Runway Meter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensor; Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; occupied stands, blocked service roads, pending pushback areas); Audit Event Ledger; Identity Access Service; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Time Synchronization Service; Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, Orchard); Business Rules Registry (BRR); Collaborative Decision Log (manual sequence changes: user, timestamp, flight, reason code); Arrival Regulation Console; Contingency Operations Console; Airline Interface Adapter; Digital Briefing Room; Alert Distribution Hub; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner (HRP; tracks dispatch/tow teams, ramp buses, loaders, stairs, GPU, air start, potable water; uses Stand Tow Request Form to reserve towing before TOBT); deicing point (requires treatment/waiting pad/under treatment/released). Tower readiness indicator combines operator, handling, cockpit, route clearance and surface position. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin); Slot Coordinator (Halcyon; CTT tolerance, Slot Compliance State); Airline Operations Coordinator (AOC, Saffron; confirms TOBT); Ground Handling Dispatcher (milestones; sends expected service completion times to HRP to separate ATC vs handling delay); Ramp Control Lead (Quartzline); Tower Supervisor (Brindle; owns sequence; must confirm revised off-block sequence compatible with Departure Metering Service

New part:
S314: The Regional Flow Platform marks a proposed Target Off Block Time as conditional when the required handling resources are forecast to arrive after the aircraft ready time.
S315: The Departure Metering Service can absorb a small ground handling variation, but repeated slips from multiple stands reduce confidence in the planned departure stream.
S316: The Aircraft Operator Representative is expected to declare whether the operator can accept a later off-block time without causing crew, connection, or aircraft rotation impacts.
S317: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the same information to decide whether a swap between company flights is operationally meaningful or merely transfers a handling bottleneck to another stand.
S318: In Normal Operations, the system assumes that typical service durations remain valid unless the Handling Resource Planner reports a constraint or the stand status stops advancing.
S319: During Adverse Weather Mode, bus turn times, loader movements, and tow availability are padded because apron driving speeds fall and personnel may be redeployed to safety duties.
S320: In the Recovery Phase, the system does not release every aircraft as soon as it becomes ready because a surge of simultaneous pushbacks can exceed tow team availability and block service roads.
S321: Each resource-driven revision is recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the reason code, revised Target Off Block Time, and affected flight identifier.
S322: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares predicted and actual handling constraints to improve standard service times and to identify chronic equipment shortages by stand group.
S323: Airspace restrictions are managed as tactical constraints that affect sector capacity, arrival acceptance, departure release timing, and the sequencing assumptions used by the Meridian regional operation.
S324: Military coordination is led through scheduled planning calls and short-notice coordination channels so that civil traffic managers receive usable timing, altitude, and boundary information before a constraint becomes active.
S325: The Military Airspace Liaison sends the Temporary Restriction Notice after confirming the activation window, affected volume, controlling authority, and any published contingency conditions.
S326: The Airspace Sector Planner converts confirmed restricted area information into sector availability assumptions and checks whether existing flight plans require rerouting, metering, or ground delay action.
S327: When a temporary restricted area reduces usable route options, the Regional Flow Manager assesses whether the effect is localized to one stream or requires a broader Ground Delay Program.
S328: The Capacity Assessment Module treats a restriction as a time-bounded reduction in route, sector, or airport throughput, depending on the geometry and operational impact of the area.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
